rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#2592: Type WebAssembly.Memory buffers as ArrayBufferLike for shared memories
rows.headline: Shared WebAssembly memories get the right buffer type
rows.description: A memory created with shared: true exposes a SharedArrayBuffer, but lib.dom said ArrayBuffer, so instanceof SharedArrayBuffer checks narrowed to never. Memory is now generic over its buffer type, and existing code keeps working.

rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#2583: Make Scheduler.postTask generic over the callback result
rows.headline: Scheduler.postTask keeps the type of your callback’s result
rows.description: postTask() returned Promise<any>, so the type of the callback’s result was lost. It is now generic, and an async callback resolves to the awaited value.

rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#2582: Add a generic createElementNS overload for the XHTML namespace
rows.headline: createElementNS returns the exact element type for XHTML
rows.description: createElementNS with the XHTML namespace returns the specific element type, like HTMLDivElement for "div", as SVG and MathML already do.

rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript-Website#3694: Document noUncheckedSideEffectImports fixes for CSS packages
rows.headline: Docs: fixing the TS2882 error on CSS imports
rows.description: Explains the TS2882 error on CSS imports since TypeScript 6.0, with fixes for library authors and for users.

rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript#61460: InstanceType and constructor return type inference for built-in Error subtypes
rows.headline: Error subtypes and InstanceType: a compatibility risk, reproduced
rows.description: Offered to implement the proposed ErrorConstructorStatics split and flagged a compatibility risk first: @types/node statics such as captureStackTrace would stop reaching TypeError, reproduced as TS2339.

rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#2566: MutationObserver.observe options should not be optional (follow-up)
rows.headline: What remains after making MutationObserver options required
rows.description: Reported that #2578 now makes observe(target) without options a compile-time error, and laid out what remains: options like {} still need a union type that would break existing code.

rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#2439: Missing bounds in WebTransportReceiveStream and WebTransportSendStream parent types
rows.headline: Byte stream types for WebTransport
rows.description: Proposed typing the receive side as ReadableStream<Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>> and the send side as WritableStream<BufferSource>, matching how other byte streams are typed and what WPT covers.

rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#2578: Make options required in MutationObserver.observe()
rows.headline: MutationObserver.observe() without options is now a compile error
rows.description: Calling observe(target) without options always throws at runtime. The DOM types now flag it at compile time.

rows.title: sindresorhus/type-fest#1285: Nullish / Nilable type
rows.headline: A Nullish type that works with exactOptionalPropertyTypes
rows.description: Showed that the proposed definition rejects an explicit undefined under exactOptionalPropertyTypes, which type-fest itself enables, and suggested adding undefined with a type test for both settings.

rows.title: sindresorhus/type-fest#1315: DeepValuesOf
rows.headline: DeepValuesOf is already expressible with Paths and Get
rows.description: Showed the request can already be expressed with Paths (leavesOnly) and Get, and listed the questions a dedicated type would need to answer: leaves only, arrays and tuples, recursion depth.

rows.title: TypeScript Performance Lab #001: Typed events: the elegant type that slowed down every call site
rows.headline: Typed events: the elegant type that slowed down every call site
rows.description: Yes. On an Apple M3 Pro (12 cores), inferring the event name from the generic parameter cut check time by 52% with TypeScript 6 and by 57% with TypeScript 7 (51% to 65% from the fastest and slowest runs); on a 1-core Intel Xeon, by 41% and 65%. The safety check passed on both machines, so the type safety is the same. Narrowing include to src also stopped TypeScript from reading a generated file the app never imports. Verified on TypeScript 6.0.3 and TypeScript 7.0.2.

rows.title: TypeScript Performance Lab #002: TypeScript 6 vs 7 on type-fest
rows.headline: TypeScript 6 vs 7 on type-fest
rows.description: On an Apple M3 Pro (12 cores), TypeScript 7.0.2 checked the type-fest sources 3.5× faster than TypeScript 6.0.3 (0.484 s vs 1.67 s): 2.6× comes from the native compiler alone (single-threaded) and 1.3× from parallel checking. On the full suite with type tests, TypeScript 6 stops at Node.js's default heap limit (4.0 GiB); with a 16 GiB heap it finishes in 74.6 s, against 14.1 s for TypeScript 7 (5.3× faster), but TypeScript 7 peaks higher in memory (11.6 GiB RSS vs 10.4 GiB). Stays open until a second machine is measured with the same protocol. Verified on TypeScript 6.0.3 and TypeScript 7.0.2.

rows.title: microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#2574: AbortSignal.any should accept an Iterable<AbortSignal>
rows.headline: Helping a first-time contributor fix AbortSignal.any
rows.description: Helped the reporter toward a fix: traced why static methods are excluded from the Iterable overloads (the generator filters them since #1839) and compared two approaches for TypeScript 6+.

rows.title: Stack Overflow: Why is the 2nd overload picked up?
rows.headline: Why TypeScript picks the second overload
rows.description: Explained that overload choice depends on the order of the checker passes, not the order of the overloads: resolveCall tries every overload with the subtype relation before falling back to assignability.
